core_obligations: Set up the base change and identify the two vanishing loci: for an object of the category, base change the algebras and the module, and rewrite each of the two closed sets where the relevant ideals generate the unit ideal as the spectrum of a tensor product of residue fields (proof lines 6117-6127).
Show the map between them is surjective: the ring map between the two tensor products is faithfully flat, so the induced map on spectra is surjective (proof lines 6128-6136).

Conclude the equality of functors: for a prime of the extended target over a prime of the extended source, flatness of the localised source module over the test algebra is equivalent to flatness of the localised target module because the extension of local rings is flat, and combining this with the surjectivity gives the equality of the two functors formally (proof lines 6137-6142).
proof_roadmap: Base change and identify the two loci (proof lines 6117-6127).
Surjectivity from faithful flatness of the residue field tensor product (proof lines 6128-6136).
Equivalence of the two flatness conditions and conclusion (proof lines 6137-6142).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the functor of points where a module is flat at a point is unchanged when the local algebra is replaced by a flat local extension and the module is extended along it (statement lines 6107-6115, tag 05II-adjacent). The proof works after an arbitrary base change: it rewrites the two relevant closed sets as spectra of tensor products of residue fields, observes that the induced map between them is surjective by faithful flatness, and then uses descent of flatness along the flat local extension to equate the two flatness conditions, concluding formally. The identification of the loci and the descent step are the substance, so the claim is H2.
